sections.html:
The Polk County Clerk of Courts keeps the Official Records. Its Public Records Searches page at polkclerkfl.gov links three searches. Official Records covers deeds, mortgages, marriage licenses, liens and HOA deed restrictions, and you can print uncertified copies at home for free.

The other two searches cover court records and tax deeds. The court search handles civil cases, criminal cases and traffic tickets, with dockets and filed documents. The tax deed search finds deeds by tax number, parcel number or sale date, and the list of lands available for taxes is on the same page.

Tax bills come from the Polk County Tax Collector at polktaxes.com. Use the clerk to see what is recorded and the tax collector to see what is owed.

sections.h2: A large county with one recorder
sections.html:
Polk covers 2,011 square miles, 1,798 of them land and 213 water, and holds 17 municipalities. The clerk records for every city and every unincorporated area. A house can sit a long drive from the clerk's offices, so the online Official Records search is the practical way to run a title check without making the trip.

That convenience helps sellers with out-of-town property and heirs handling a house from afar. You can read the chain of recorded documents tonight, print what you need, and decide what to ask the clerk by phone tomorrow.

Page one costs $10.00 and each page after that $8.50, for an instrument up to 14 by 8.5 inches. Indexing a document with more than four names adds $1.00 per additional name. The clerk's fee page notes that the Florida Legislature regulates court fees, not the clerk's office.

Property-related charges at the Polk County Clerk

Cash, credit card, money order and check are all accepted, and credit cards carry a service charge. A veteran's certificate of discharge is recorded at no cost to the veteran.

The rate is seventy cents for every $100 of consideration, in effect since August 1, 1992. The clerk's fee page also prints earlier rates, from 10 cents per $100 for November 1931 to June 1957 up to 60 cents per $100 for June 1991 to July 1992, which is handy when you read an old deed.

The Florida Department of Revenue says all parties to a deed are liable for the tax, whichever party agrees to pay. Consideration includes a mortgage the buyer takes subject to, assumed or not. Warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds, a contract for deed and a deed in place of foreclosure are all taxable. A spousal homestead deed whose only consideration is a mortgage is exempt, and so is a divorce deed for the marital home.

Section 689.01 requires a deed to be in writing and signed in front of two witnesses. Ask your closing agent to confirm the witnessing before the document goes to the clerk.

sections.h2: Court fees that matter to a distressed owner
sections.html:
Owners facing foreclosure, an inherited house or a problem tenant will meet other clerk charges. A judicial sale, with recording of the certificate of sale and title, costs $70.00, and an electronic sale adds another $70.00.

  • Removal of a tenant, county civil: $185.00.
  • Opening an estate: $231.00. Summary administration is $235.00 for estates under $1,000 and $345.00 at $1,000 or more. Formal administration is $400.00.
  • Starting a real property action: $400.00 under $50,000 of property value, $905.00 from $50,000 to $250,000, and $1,905.00 over $250,000, each needing a written estimate of value.
  • Release of a lis pendens: $10.00 on page one and $8.50 on later pages.

Florida's estate tax ended for people who died after December 31, 2004, and personal representatives have not needed to file Form DR-312 or DR-313 since July 1, 2023. Summary administration is available if the nonexempt estate does not exceed $150,000, or if the decedent has been dead more than two years.

Free home printing covers uncertified copies only. A certified copy adds $2.00 for certification, plus $1.00 for each photographic copy up to 14 by 8.5 inches and $5.00 for a larger one.

When clerk staff search for you, the charge is $2.00 per year searched. A notary service costs $10, an oath is $3.50 and a validated or exemplified certificate is $7.00. Transferring a lien to security is $20.00, with $10.00 for each added lien on the same security.

The clerk also sells self-help books for people filing without a lawyer, at $15.00 to $25.00, and the fee page gives 863-534-4015 for them. If you need a record for a VA benefit claim, section 744.637 of the Florida Statutes provides a certified copy at no charge.

sections.h2: What to check in the records before you sell
sections.html:
Search the owner's name and the property description, and read every recorded item against the property. The buyer's closing agent runs the same search, so see the results before you list.

  • Mortgages with no recorded release.
  • Liens and judgments filed against the owner.
  • HOA deed restrictions, which the Official Records search covers.
  • Any tax deed or tax certificate activity, using the tax deed search.

A sale is a change of ownership for property tax, so the assessment resets to market value on the next January 1, with exceptions such as a transfer between spouses. Tell your buyer to expect a bill built on the sale value, and ask the Polk property appraiser or tax collector for the current figures on your parcel.

Print the search results, circle anything unresolved and sort it by who can fix it. A lender can record a missing release. A lienholder can give a written payoff. A court clerk can tell you what a judgment says. A title agent can tell you which items a buyer's lender will insist on seeing cleared. Ask early, because each fix has its own turnaround, and several fixes in parallel finish sooner than several in a row. Bring the fixes to the title agent at the same time so the closing is not held up by a late surprise.

The same records matter in a cash sale. A buyer paying cash still wants clear title, and the title company still searches these same records before it will issue a policy.

faqs.q: Who is the recorder in Polk County?
faqs.a: The Polk County Clerk of Courts. The Official Records search lists deeds, mortgages, liens, marriage licenses and HOA deed restrictions.

faqs.q: Can I print Polk County records for free?
faqs.a: Yes, uncertified copies from the Official Records, court records and tax deed searches can be printed at home for free. Certified copies cost $2.00 for the certification.

faqs.q: What is the first page recording fee in Polk County?
faqs.a: Page one costs $10.00 and each page after it costs $8.50. Instruments with more than four names add $1.00 per additional name.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp tax rate in Polk County?
faqs.a: Seventy cents for every $100 of consideration, in effect since August 1, 1992. All parties to the deed are liable for it.

faqs.q: How many municipalities are in Polk County?
faqs.a: There are 17, but one clerk records for every city and every unincorporated area. The county covers 2,011 square miles, of which 1,798 are land.
